full_story_part1.canonical_text:
I was impressed: “AI can even make phone calls. The future is here!” But the person handling the request on the other end of the line was human. Wait—what a sudden change of genre, from science fiction to a workplace drama. Still, the heart of this story is not “So it was a human after all!” It is whether people were properly told about the change in who was taking part.

Meta was testing some calls made through Muse in which trained contract workers made the calls and completed the conversations with the other person. They tested a setup where Muse handed the work over to a human agent. Not all calls were handled by humans. It’s too soon to put up a caption saying, “Actually, it was all done by people!”

full_story_part2.text: But one important notice was missing from this test. The vice president of Meta's Superintelligence Labs division admitted in an internal post that starting a test in which contract workers made calls without proper disclosure was a mistake. The vice president also said that Meta had rolled back its human concierge feature for now. Let's check the breaking-news caption once more. What they pulled back was the human concierge feature. They did not stop all calls through Muse. Canceling an entire show and pausing one segment are 2 different things. So, is it bad in itself to bring in a human helper? There may be times when handing things to a person helps move the conversation forward. But there is a big difference between telling someone, A person will take over from here, and quietly changing the cast backstage. In a movie, you might clap and say, Ah, so that's who it is! when a mysterious person is revealed. But you may not want a surprise reveal in a conversation you are part of.

full_story_part2.canonical_text:
But one important notice was missing from this test. The vice president of Meta’s Superintelligence Labs division admitted in an internal post that starting a test in which contract workers made calls without proper disclosure was a “mistake.” The vice president also said that Meta had rolled back its human concierge feature for now.

Let’s check the breaking-news caption once more. What they pulled back was the human concierge feature. They did not stop all calls through Muse. Canceling an entire show and pausing one segment are two different things.

So, is it bad in itself to bring in a human helper? There may be times when handing things to a person helps move the conversation forward. But there is a big difference between telling someone, “A person will take over from here,” and quietly changing the cast backstage. In a movie, you might clap and say, “Ah, so that’s who it is!” when a mysterious person is revealed. But you may not want a surprise reveal in a conversation you are part of.

full_story_part3.text: Some people may choose their words or feel differently when they think they are talking to AI than when they know they are talking to a person. Even if the request is handled without a problem, that does not mean the disclosure issue can be brushed aside with it all worked out in the end. That was exactly the point Meta itself admitted it had got wrong. Convenience matters. But for some people, knowing who they are talking to matters just as much. If AI hands the baton to a person, that one line saying so is part of the service, too. The person taking over does not have to be a secret guest.
